title: Koopman operator-augmented physics-informed neural network with SEI kinetics for stable and explainable SOH estimation in battery packs
abstract: Accurate estimation of State of Health (SOH) is pivotal for battery management, yet existing data-driven methods often lack physical interpretability and struggle with generalization under complex operating conditions. To bridge the gap between data-driven flexibility and electrochemical mechanism consistency, this paper proposes a Koopman Operator-Augmented Physics-Informed Neural Network (Koopman-PINN) tailored for battery pack SOH estimation. Unlike traditional black-box models, the proposed method embeds the nonlinear SOH degradation into a high-dimensional Koopman observation space where it evolves linearly. Crucially, the Solid Electrolyte Interphase (SEI) growth kinetics and boundedness conditions are embedded as physical loss terms. A spectral domain constraint is further imposed on the Koopman operator matrix, which forces all eigenvalues inside the unit circle (|λi| < 1) and constrains their phase angles to guarantee the physical consistency and long-term stability of the degradation trajectory. Furthermore, the SEI degradation rate coefficient α is treated as an independent trainable parameter, enabling the end-to-end learning of physical parameters. Validated on extensive battery pack datasets under quasi-constant temperature (804 cycles) and variable temperature (667 cycles) conditions, the Koopman-PINN reduces the MAE by 46.0% and RMSE by 48.9% compared to standard PINNs in quasi-constant temperature. Under variable temperature conditions, Koopman-PINN reduces MAE by 30.0% and RMSE by 29.6% compared to the traditional PINN. Notably, the learned activation energy (≈30 kJ/mol) aligns well with the physical laws of SEI growth, and the spectral analysis reveals distinct dynamical modes governing the degradation process, providing a novel interpretable perspective on battery aging mechanisms.
title_zh: Koopman operator-augmented physics-informed neural network with SEI kinetics for stable and explainable SOH estimation in battery packs

title: Evaluating Deep Learning Models for Lithium-Ion Battery RUL Prediction via Unified Benchmarks: A Comparative Study
abstract: Lithium-ion battery remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for the safe and efficient operation of energy storage systems. Traditional physics-based and empirical data-driven methods rely heavily on expert knowledge and predefined degradation models, limiting their generalizability across diverse operating conditions. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as a powerful alternative, automatically learning features from raw sensor data without requiring explicit electrochemical assumptions. However, comparative studies of deep learning models for RUL prediction remain fragmented due to inconsistent benchmarks and preprocessing protocols. To address this, we present a unified evaluation of 24 models from six architectural families using the NASA PCoE battery dataset, covering multiple temperatures and discharge currents. All models share standardized inputs and preprocessing, including moving average smoothing with a window of 45 cycles to attenuate measurement noise. Evaluation covers prediction accuracy (RMSE, MAE, R2, MAPE, SMAPE, MedAE) and computational efficiency, with Pareto frontier analysis. Results show that WaveNet achieves the best overall performance (RMSE = 0.0194, R2 = 0.9834), followed by TCN (RMSE = 0.0247) and CNN (RMSE = 0.0307), while performance varies across families depending on the specific architecture and data regime. This study provides, for the first time, a systematic benchmark and practical guidance for deep learning model selection in battery health management.
title_zh: Evaluating Deep Learning Models for Lithium-Ion Battery RUL Prediction via Unified Benchmarks: A Comparative Study
